name: Anarcho-Naturism
summary: Anarcho-naturism (naturianism, libertarian naturism) fuses anarchism with a return to natural life. Its founders in 1890s Paris rejected every legally established power and politics, accepting only the laws of nature, and condemned industrial civilization, progress and machines as domineering, urging limited needs, self-sufficiency and nudism. It was a loose current that spread to Spain and Cuba, not a systematic programme.
scope: The French naturian current of Émile Gravelle, Henri Zisly and Henri Beylie (journals L'État Naturel, Le Naturien, La Vie Naturelle), with the Spanish and Cuban anarchist naturism it influenced. Excludes mainstream apolitical naturism and nudism as leisure, and later anarcho-primitivism. Most economic and social-policy questions are not addressed in the sources, so many answers are inferences from its anarchism and anti-industrialism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Naturians sought health through natural living and self-reliance and rejected state power, so a state-run health system is unlikely to be endorsed; inferred, since medicine is not discussed in the sources.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage labour and legal regulation by a state are outside the naturian project of self-sufficient living; a wage floor is an inference from their rejection of legal power.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Zisly's ideal of limited needs and self-sufficiency points away from commerce as the organising principle; not stated directly, and naturians were not market advocates either.

public-ownership.rationale: Naturians reject every legally established power, so state ownership of industry is excluded; they also oppose industrial infrastructure itself.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation presupposes a state they oppose, though hostility to wealth is likely; adherents would more likely reject the whole fiscal apparatus than demand higher rates.

unions-good.rationale: Anarcho-naturists in Cuba and Spain moved among anarcho-syndicalist circles, but the naturians' own writings focus on a return to nature rather than industrial unions, so adherents are split or indifferent.

property-fundamental.rationale: As anarchists opposed to legally established power they reject legal enforcement of property rights, though some individualists among them valued personal self-sufficiency; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations are products of the industrial civilization they oppose, but regulation would be state action; adherents would want them gone rather than regulated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Naturians reject the state but nothing in the sources says they favour cutting welfare as a policy; the statement's dependency framing is foreign to them.

worker-ownership.rationale: Naturians placed themselves among moderate libertarians who set aside part of anarchist-communist doctrine; factory ownership matters little to a movement rejecting industry.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Opposition to all legally established power and politics makes state surveillance unacceptable.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Naturians included both temperate and abstinent members regarding alcohol and tobacco, so legal status of drugs is not a settled naturian position; anti-prohibition follows from anarchism but natural-health ideals pull the other way.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anarchists reject legal coercion and state censorship; inferred from opposition to legal power, not discussed in the sources.

strong-leader.rationale: Zisly states naturians fight all legally established power; a leader bypassing gridlock is the opposite of their anarchism.

state-harmful.rationale: Zisly describes naturians as anarchists in politics, opposed to all legally established power and all politics, accepting only the laws of nature.

limit-guns.rationale: Anarchists oppose state monopoly of force but naturians say little about arms; some are revolutionaries and some not.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and military are instruments of the legal power naturians fight.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Naturism's anarchist branch resisted state and church authority over the body, but the sources say nothing on commercial sex; adherents' views are unknown.

decide-locally.rationale: Their ideal of small-scale self-sufficient living implies local autonomy; stated only indirectly through promotion of limited needs and self-sufficiency.

rehabilitation.rationale: Rejecting the legal order, naturians would not defend punishment; rehabilitation is an inference as prisons are not discussed.

traditional-family.rationale: Koch's naturist movement challenged parental, church and state authority, which suggests scepticism of traditional structures; family views are inferred, not stated.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anarchists oppose state-conferred marriage as such, so a legalisation demand does not fit; the sources do not address it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the naturian sources; anarchist rejection of legal control over the body suggests support, but this is only an inference.

more-religion-public.rationale: Zisly says naturians are all materialists and rejects religious adherence; religion in public life is opposed, as is every established power.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; naturians reject state programmes, though anarchists generally oppose racism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; naturians appeal to natural laws, which pulls against pure social constructionism, while anarchism pulls toward it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Anarchists reject nations as legal powers, and naturians value the natural over the customary; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Zisly notes naturians included both revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries, but adherents reject respect for established institutions as such; inferred.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Hostile to state borders as legal power; inferred, as migration is not discussed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International bodies are legal powers above states; the naturian rejection of all legal power covers them.

free-trade.rationale: Naturians promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency over commerce, though anarchists oppose tariffs as state acts; inferred.

nation-first.rationale: Anarchists reject the nation-state as an authority; naturians have no stated nationalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military action is a state power that naturians reject; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Naturians include nomads, and anarchists oppose state borders; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs, self-sufficiency and a return to natural life while denouncing progress, which implies opposing endless economic growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Naturians would oppose industrial causes but also state-led action; split by their rejection of government.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Zisly called progress and civilization absurd and saw machines as inherently domineering, and says victims of technology are victims of Progress.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is an extreme case of the industrial machinery Zisly opposed, though not discussed directly.

revolution-justified.rationale: Zisly notes naturians included both revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries, so support is not universal, but anarchist politics generally accepts revolution as justified.

experts-over-public.rationale: Naturians called themselves anti-scientific anarchists and reject authority, so rule by experts is rejected.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning is state power over industry; both the anarchism and the anti-industrialism of naturians reject it.

socialized-markets.rationale: Naturians do not address markets with worker ownership; they would treat industry as the main problem.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax implies a state; naturians do not advocate fiscal schemes.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Taxation is a state power they reject; hostility to inherited wealth is plausible but not documented.

basic-income.rationale: A state payment contradicts their rejection of legal power; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protecting industry combines state action with the industrialism that Zisly opposed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of industry is rejected both as state power and as support for industrial civilization.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Self-sufficiency fits small holdings, but anarchists reject legally enforced property; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anarchist communists in the movement wanted abolition, but Zisly described naturians as differing from anarchist communism on some points; not settled.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Banks are not discussed; they reject the state yet are not market anarchists.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies setting wages are legal powers that naturians reject.

one-party-rule.rationale: Zisly states naturians oppose all legally established power and all politics, which excludes a ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Zisly fought all legally established power, which clearly implies rejecting hereditary monarchy, though he does not discuss it.

democracy-best.rationale: Naturians oppose parliamentarism and all politics according to Zisly's account; they are not democrats in the representative sense.

direct-votes.rationale: Anarchists prefer voluntary consensus to voting under a state, but direct votes beat representation; split.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils are an anarcho-syndicalist idea; naturians are less concerned with industrial workplaces, so not a stated position.

right-to-secede.rationale: Decentralist and anti-state outlook implies sympathy; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: Naturians accept no authority besides natural law and reject all established power.

political-violence-never.rationale: Naturians included revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries, so views on violence were divided; absolute pacifism is not their stated line, though a pacifist current existed later.

war-builds-character.rationale: Naturism became associated with pacifism in Germany and anarchist naturists opposed war; the glorification of war conflicts with natural-life ideals.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anarchists reject the state, and Zisly rejects religious adherence; strict separation is inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Zisly accepts only the laws of nature, rejects religion, and rejects legal power.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Naturians are not market anarchists; they reject legal power in general, and no private-defence stance is documented.

military-superiority.rationale: Military power is a legal-authority structure opposed by naturians.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Anarchists reject nations as states; naturians say nothing favouring ethnic nationhood.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Zisly distanced naturians from the scientific claims of anarchist communism; not a stated naturian thesis.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; their stress on natural life and nomadism might sympathise, but this is not documented.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; reparations require state action.

civilizational-union.rationale: Political unions are legal powers that naturians oppose, and they denounce civilization.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Naturian anarchism descended from individualist anarchism, but they stress harmony with nature, so adherents are split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Naturians reject externally imposed authority; duty-first communitarianism is not their ethic.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Naturians hold that the laws of nature are the only valid ones and that people should adapt themselves to nature rather than fight it, which points to valuing nature itself.

limit-population.rationale: Neo-Malthusian circles overlapped with anarchism, but population limits by the state would conflict with naturians' rejection of legal power.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Zisly opposed industrialization and machines and condemned progress and civilization as ignoble; Gravelle's naturianism set a free natural state against industrial civilization.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Zisly saw machines as inherently domineering and rejected progress, so speeding up technological change is the reverse of his aims.

human-enhancement.rationale: They call for adapting to nature, but they also stand for bodily freedom; enhancement through technology runs against their anti-technological outlook.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by algorithms is anachronistic for a 1890s-1910 current; rejection is inferred from its hostility to government and machinery.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; freedom from state surveillance fits, but it relies on technology they dislike.

restore-past-order.rationale: Naturians looked back to a natural prehistoric state, not to a lost social order; the statement's traditional-order sense does not fit.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Naturians treat the laws of nature as a doctrine; pragmatism is not their outlook.

direct-action.rationale: They reject parliamentarism and all politics; Zisly says naturians fight established power and combine practical lifestyle action with propaganda.

means-match-ends.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and practical self-sufficient living as the way to a natural life, aligning means with the intended society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Zisly advocated a return to natural life with limited needs and self-sufficiency; naturian currents were nomadic and sedentary, and some saw prehistory as abundant, but not every adherent urged full foraging.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Self-sufficiency suggests less specialisation, but no source says the division of labour should be abolished.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Zisly separated naturians from anarchist communism on some points; not addressed.

production-for-use.rationale: Limited needs and self-sufficiency imply production for use over profit; inferred.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Not stated by naturians; Zisly kept distance from anarchist-communist doctrine.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Zisly and the naturiens never addressed this; rejection of any dictatorship is inferred from their anarchism.

collective-farming.rationale: Both nomadic and sedentary naturians existed and self-sufficiency could be individual or communal; split.

taxation-theft.rationale: Anarchists reject the state and thus its taxes, though naturians made no known fiscal argument.

harm-principle.rationale: Anarchists reject state restriction broadly; naturians appeal to natural law rather than a harm principle.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Individualist anarchist origins suggest yes, but a nature-centred outlook gives no stated view on group rights.

conscription.rationale: Conscription is state coercion that naturians, opposed to all legally established power, reject.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; they reject both voting politics and the state.

state-as-business.rationale: They reject government itself, not a business model for it.

media-academia-power.rationale: The naturian sources never rank media or academia against elected officials; they reject all politics, so the comparison has no stated answer.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Naturians are anarchists who rejected hierarchy; nothing in sources endorses racial genetic hierarchy.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation of any kind through bodies is political authority they reject.

total-state.rationale: Anarchist rejection of the state clearly implies rejecting the total state, though no source states it.

national-rebirth.rationale: A nationalist theme alien to naturians who reject states and politics.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Their rejection of state power clearly implies opposing state expansion, though no source discusses it.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by oaths of loyalty is a legal power they reject.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour is coercion opposed by all anarchists, including naturians.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Zisly's anti-scientific stance suggests scepticism, but the claim about power and truth is not stated.

universal-morality.rationale: They appeal to natural laws as universal, though the statement concerns reason-found moral truths; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Naturians reject political authority to define a common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anarchists oppose states; not addressed specifically.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship and return rights are state categories on which the naturian sources are silent; a neutral midpoint reflects indifference.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival as state policy is not naturian; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; workplaces mean industry they oppose.

school-vouchers.rationale: A state programme; they would reject state schooling and its funding mechanisms.

economic-freedom.rationale: Naturians treat freedom as natural life rather than economic freedom; not addressed.

rule-by-example.rationale: Naturians reject rulers altogether, whatever their example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anarchists reject states, yet decentralist sympathies exist; split.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of state military force abroad is opposed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Zisly called naturians anti-scientific anarchists who follow the laws of nature; they also reject religion, so emotion and nature, not reason alone, guide them.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Citizenship is a legal category they reject; not addressed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: State conditions on welfare are legal coercion; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Zisly kept naturians apart from anarchist-communist doctrine and wrote nothing on class partnership or conflict, so no side is documented.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Anti-civilization but not committed to destroying libraries; Zisly condemned civilization, yet this is not stated.

dominated-front.rationale: Alliances of states against Western powers are never discussed; naturians, hostile to states, have no stated geopolitical bloc view.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism of workers is inconsistent with their anti-state outlook.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Naturist nudism challenged conditioning by church, parents and state in Koch's movement, and anarchists reject legally fixed roles; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Usury law is not mentioned by Zisly or Gravelle; a legal ban is state action, while hostility to commerce pulls the other way, so it nets to neutral.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation by law is state power their anarchism rejects; implied, not stated.

state-class-instrument.rationale: As anarchists who see legal power as the enemy, they would hold that the state serves domination, though the sources do not phrase it in class terms.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Industrial extraction is part of the industrial civilization Zisly opposed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Forced assimilation is state coercion; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in any naturian source; anarchist egalitarian outlook rejects it.

proportional-representation.rationale: They reject parliamentary politics altogether, so voting reforms are not their goal.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a government form by a state is contrary to their rejection of states.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Naturist anarchists were prominent in sexual emancipation, but no source states a structural patriarchy thesis for naturians.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Hostile to politics and political power; corruption claim is inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State eugenics is coercive legal power that anarchists reject.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Naturians reject the state, so legal accountability is not their method.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Any state, even minimal, is a legally established power they oppose.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Their rejection of coercive social norms clearly implies opposing this, though no source discusses it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anarchist egalitarian outlook that rejects hierarchical authority supports equal worth, though the sources do not discuss it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist debate about revolution and borders that the naturian sources never enter.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: No naturian source discusses settlement or colonial states; the question is left without a documented answer.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Legal uniformity is a state project; anarchists reject civil law as such.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Zisly rejects religious adherence and legal power; law restricting belief is a coercion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Vegetarians and omnivores were both naturians, so no ban would be stated; a legal ban is also state power.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: They reject state and religion alike; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The Stalinist doctrine postdates the movement; rejection is inferred from its anti-state view.

consent-of-governed.rationale: They accept no political authority as legitimate; consent theory does not fit.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export orientation belongs to industrial commerce they oppose.

population-transfer.rationale: State expulsion of minorities is coercion their anarchism rejects; implied, not stated.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Naturians reject progress itself and favour adaptation to nature.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They oppose legal power over politics, and also reject party politics generally.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Zisly saw machines and powers as domineering and rejected legal authority, matching a freedom-from-domination view though not named.

separated-powers.rationale: They reject every legally established power rather than dividing it.

vanguard-party.rationale: Zisly and the naturiens never addressed this; rejection of a disciplined leading party is inferred from their anarchism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The sources give no stance on laws prioritising the poor, since naturians reject legal institutions altogether.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a state welfare device that the naturian sources never mention.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Legal restriction of labour action is state power they oppose.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The naturian sources do not explain poverty by population or by institutions; they blame industrial civilization generally, which fits neither side.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Not documented; anarchist universalism rejects it.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: They reject public offices; lottery is not a stated preference.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are state authority they oppose; implied, not stated.

party-controls-media.rationale: Party and online media control are later questions; rejection is inferred from the naturiens' hostility to authority.

party-commands-army.rationale: Their rejection of all established power clearly implies rejecting this, though no source discusses it.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship bureaucracy is a state power they reject.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: They reject representation, so the pay level is moot.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline is an organisational authority they reject.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They reject sovereignty at all levels.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of armed force is state power they reject; implied, not stated.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Zisly rejects religious adherence; no stance on church governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Clerics holding authority are opposed by materialist anarchist naturians.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anarchists generally oppose state war; naturians' war views are inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: They reject offices; recall is moot.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are state institutions; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not discussed; self-sufficient living might favour owning a plot but nothing states a ban on renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; some anarchists favour militias, naturians gave no view.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Zisly urged a return to natural life, limited needs and self-sufficiency and condemned civilization; the naturist movement was built on health through nature and open air.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National unification through states is not their aim.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Zisly's anti-scientific stance suggests suspicion of learned culture, but not documented as such.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not addressed; they favour natural over civilised life, which ranks ways of life.

death-penalty.rationale: State execution is a legal power they reject.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Koch's naturist work aimed at freeing children from authority-imposed conditioning, but state curricula are not endorsed; split and inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Naturians are materialists and reject religious authority.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Naturism is generally promoted as non-sexual, but anarchists reject state restriction of expression; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are state law they reject.

minority-language-support.rationale: State language policy is not covered by the naturian sources.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They oppose religion and law alike; exemptions are a legal construct.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Naturist anarchists defended nudity and unconventional living, and Koch used nudity to challenge conditioning by authority; adherents would welcome non-conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: International sovereign debt is a state-finance question absent from naturian writings.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The naturian sources do not treat national independence movements at all.

constituent-assembly.rationale: They oppose parliamentary politics and constitutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Both their anarchism and their hostility to industrial growth clearly imply rejection; not stated.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State foreign aid is not discussed; naturians' stress on self-sufficiency and rejection of states cancel out.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; rejection is inferred from its anti-state and anti-industrial views.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: They reject heads of state altogether.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Territorial claims by states are not theirs.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is not discussed; split between individualist and communal strands.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; anarchists generally reject Soviet state but naturians left no record.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Their stress on adapting to nature suggests caution about industrial risks; the state mechanism is a problem.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The naturian sources do not address annexation or international law.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They reject both state and church; making the church subject to the state is not their method.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: They reject heads of state as such, which clearly implies disagreement; not stated.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: State force to hold territory is what their anarchism rejects; implied, not stated.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Special autonomy within a larger state is a constitutional question outside the naturian sources.

flat-income-tax.rationale: They reject taxation as part of the state.

character-from-environment.rationale: Gravelle and Zisly blamed civilization for corrupting people and held that natural living frees them, which implies environment shapes character.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Their opposition to all established power clearly implies rejecting an unbound ruler; not stated.

space-expansion.rationale: Space programmes epitomise the progress and industry Zisly rejected.

mixed-constitution.rationale: They reject constitutions and political rule.

leader-cult.rationale: Their opposition to rulers and authority clearly implies rejecting leader veneration; not stated.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed, and naturians reject courts and legal rules over private life, leaving no clear answer.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A debate internal to state socialism that naturians, distinct from anarchist communism, never joined.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; return to land suggests sympathy but is not stated.

refugee-return.rationale: The right of return of expelled populations is not addressed in the naturian sources.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: State territorial claims are foreign to their anti-state anarchism; implied, not stated.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Rejects both religious adherence and legal power.

women-must-cover.rationale: Naturiens defended nudity as bodily freedom and rejected legal compulsion, so opposition to a covering mandate is inferred; no source discusses it.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are state monetary arrangements that the naturian sources do not mention.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Political unions among peoples are state-building.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority institutions within states are a nationality-policy question absent from naturian writings.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Naturians say nothing on minority strategy toward statehood or emigration.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Not stated by naturians who distanced themselves from anarchist-communist scientific claims.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposed to state spending on firms; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject courts and majority rule alike.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Self-sufficiency is a naturian ideal at personal level; a state economic bloc would not be.

moral-incentives.rationale: A life of limited needs and natural living implies noncommercial motives; not stated for work incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Naturians had revolutionary and non-revolutionary members, so views on armed groups vary.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to all established power and privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Naturians denounce civilization, so teaching history around a civilization's centre does not fit; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Zisly called civilization and progress ignoble, so ruling others to civilise them is rejected, besides being domination.

patriotic-education.rationale: State schooling in loyalty is legal power and nationalism they reject.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Admissions and hiring policy is not a subject of the naturian sources.

public-money-creation.rationale: A state institution; they offer no monetary scheme.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Zisly distanced naturians from the scientific claims of anarchist communism, and no source gives a naturian theory of capitalist crisis.

delink-world-market.rationale: Self-sufficiency and limited needs fit delinking in spirit; inferred.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: The Marxist thesis on rich-country workers is not discussed by naturians.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Individualist roots suggest freedom of association, but no stated view; also hostility to hierarchy.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutions are legal power; they accept only natural laws.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial border treaties are not addressed in the sources.

minority-veto.rationale: Anarchist individualism implies no one is bound without consent; inferred.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Resistance to authority fits, but they reject rulers altogether, not just lawless ones.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Naturians fight parliamentarism per Zisly's account of their politics.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Vegetarians were among naturians, but Zisly called vegetarianism anti-scientific and others ate meat, so this is an inference from nature-centred ethics.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Naturians included both vegetarians and omnivores according to Zisly, so views on animal use were split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchical duty of the privileged is opposed to anarchist egalitarianism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Zisly says naturians oppose all politics and favour a natural life of self-sufficiency; withdrawing into it fits, though they also propagandised.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Hostility to civilization and its institutions suggests this; not directly sourced.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: No naturian source offers a theory of how ruling classes keep consent; they simply reject all established power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not addressed; naturians criticise industrial civilization, not core-periphery exchange.

native-born-offices.rationale: They reject public offices and legal citizenship.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Self-sufficiency is a naturian ideal, though applied to individuals not countries.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: They reject political leadership of any group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Opposed to fascism as authoritarian, but they reject constitutions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Naturians pre-date the debate; they oppose all legal power, but no source rates fascism against communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; any anarchist rejects slavery, and the historical claim is inferred negatively.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: They reject official commemoration of states and rulers; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Public programmes for boys and men are not addressed by the naturian sources.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The naturian sources do not address domestic violence or its policy treatment.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Naturians reject the state everywhere, so they say nothing on which civilization suits which institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military authority is state power they reject; implied, not stated.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wage labour framing; they promote self-sufficiency over waged labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Imposed duties conflict with anarchist anti-authoritarianism.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Anarchist rejection of church and state authority over private life suggests free dissolution of unions; marriage is not discussed in the sources.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private financial products are outside their self-sufficient lifestyle, and state pensions are rejected too.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed directly; split between individual and communal land among strands.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: They reject parliament and the state budget.

single-official-language.rationale: State imposition of language is a legal power.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; borders are not recognised by anarchists.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Discrimination law is not discussed, and naturians reject legal doctrines generally.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency and condemned civilization; the movement stressed simple living.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: A state military act they reject.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Their anti-state anarchism clearly implies rejecting great-power intervention, though no source discusses it.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not addressed beyond opposition to commercial civilization.

residents-only-property.rationale: A legal restriction by state authorities.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state employment programme, and wage employment in industry.

democratic-peace.rationale: The sources do not take up this international-relations thesis; naturians reject parliamentary democracy while opposing war, so it is neutral.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Zisly states naturians recognise only natural law and oppose all legally established power, so legal duty to obey is denied.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to states, so also to their interventions, but the strict principle is not stated.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not stated; anarcho-syndicalist circles that included naturists favoured them but naturians themselves were anti-industrial.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not found in any source; contrary to anarchist egalitarianism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Anarchists reject state-conferred status and the sources show naturism challenging church and state authority over private life; marriage itself is not discussed, so inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: They reject the state, so legal rights are not their frame.

local-production.rationale: Self-sufficiency and limited needs, as promoted by Zisly, imply producing near where goods are consumed.

informal-organisation.rationale: Spanish naturists were an affinity group among anarcho-syndicalists and French naturians worked through small journals and circles; informal grouping fits.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Both are legal powers; neither is accepted.

religious-nation.rationale: Zisly says all naturians are materialists who reject religion, so defining a nation by religion has no place in their outlook.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Hierarchy among states is rejected by their anarchism; implied, not stated.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Self-sufficient living implies personal belongings; the statement's means-of-production side is not addressed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-authoritarian and not anti-communist in a Cold War sense; hostile to state communism but not seeking its defeat.

religion-illusion.rationale: Zisly says all naturians are materialists, but the consolation theory of religion is not stated.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Zisly rejects progress and civilization in the industrial commercial form.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The naturian sources do not discuss women's equality in relation to the economy.

socialized-care.rationale: Public services are state action; they favour self-sufficient living.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with indigenous nations are not covered in naturian writings.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Historian Beaudet links the early-twentieth-century free communities of French individualist anarchists to the Naturians, and naturist clubs commonly share work and land; communities fit, though property-in-common is not stated.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-directed settlement is coercion their anarchism rejects; implied, not stated.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Zisly separated naturians from anarchist communism on some matters and opposed commerce, but they also place themselves among anarchists; position not stated in this form.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Claims of states or peoples to land are not accepted by anarchists.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The movement ended before the Holocaust, so the question is anachronistic; rejection of denial is inferred from anarchist egalitarianism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Naturiens challenged church and state power over the body; opposition to criminal law on same-sex relations is inferred, not stated.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is the authoritarianism they fought; implied, not stated.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Zisly's account has naturians fighting all legally established power, which rules out civil punishment of religious speech or practice.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Imperial domination is contrary to their anarchism; implied, not stated.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious military duty contradicts their materialism; not addressed.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Theocratic revolution is contrary to materialist naturians.

participatory-democracy.rationale: They reject parliamentary politics, but direct participation in communities fits; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The concept of overlapping oppressions post-dates the naturians and is absent from their writings.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; they reject legal recognition as state action.

assisted-dying.rationale: End-of-life medicine is not discussed; their trust in natural living and their opposition to legal control cut in different directions.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Zisly placed naturians within anarchism and libertarianism, and no source says they reject the left-right axis.

alienated-labor.rationale: Hostility to machines as domineering and industrial civilization suggests alienation; this is an inference from Zisly's critique.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not found in any source; contrary to anarchist egalitarianism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: They are materialists who reject religious adherence and legal power.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: They reject the state; the statement concerns state rules that they would not make.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Employment-contract regulation is not addressed by the naturian sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: A state-regulated industrial economy that they reject.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Military power is part of legal authority they fight, and naturism was linked with pacifism in Germany.

rich-first.rationale: They want limited needs, not growth; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: They reject states and blocs; neutrality is an inference.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary rule is a legal power they fight.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; mutualist ideas are individualist anarchism but not shown for naturians.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The IMF and international lending are modern state-finance matters absent from the naturian sources.

property-franchise.rationale: They oppose legal voting systems and class restrictions.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Their nature-centred critique of domination of life fits, but the connection is not stated by the sources.

reification.rationale: The Marxist theory of commodity fetishism is not part of naturian writings, which attack industry and machines rather than commodity relations.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Press ownership is not discussed; naturians' own journals were small and self-published, but they gave no analysis of the issue.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They recognise only natural laws and reject legal power.

racial-franchise.rationale: A racial franchise is contrary to anarchist equality; implied, not stated.

online-participation.rationale: Online politics is both politics and technology that naturians reject.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Legal control of personal relations is state power they reject; opposition is inferred, not stated.

citizens-assembly.rationale: They reject political deliberative bodies as a form of politics.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Naturians reject religion rather than reforming it, but the statement is about religious adherents.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: They fight established power and oppose commercial civilization; wealth as power would be included.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: They reject armed forces; not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: They are materialists but reject state power, so state promotion is excluded.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: They oppose all legally established power, which includes police and prisons.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not rank charity against state aid, though mutual aid might fit anarchism.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; their anti-technology view might sympathise, but this is not stated.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: They reject religion, so not their issue.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: They reject legal marriage authority altogether; the statement presumes marriage law.

abolish-ip.rationale: Anarchists generally oppose legal monopolies; inferred.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national-service youth is state militarism they reject; implied, not stated.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Opposes arms and industrial technology; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of past killings is a state act on which naturians are silent.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Distribution of income is not addressed in the naturian sources.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Views on violence varied among naturians, who included revolutionaries and anti-revolutionaries.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Naturians appealed to natural law and the body, and no source engages with the constructionist claim about sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory of categories is not part of naturian writings.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Zisly says all naturians are materialists.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Zionist-style homeland debates are not touched by the naturian sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: National cultural renewal is outside the naturian sources, which reject the state outright.

god-not-male.rationale: Zisly rejects religion as such, so intra-religious debate about divine language is not their concern.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist theology is outside the naturians' materialist rejection of religion.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic economic control is contrary to anarchism.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative unification by states is not theirs.

independent-unions.rationale: If unions exist, anarchist circles want them independent of the state; naturians themselves said little.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A debate about what counts as socialism, which naturians as non-socialist anarchists did not take up.

municipal-property.rationale: Not addressed; between individual and communal property.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Not addressed for naturians; federal anarchist structure is common but unstated.

family-wage.rationale: Wage-based industrial framing; not their ideal.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Naturians favoured natural living and were anti-scientific per Zisly, and approvals are regulatory power.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Technological research funded by government is contrary to their anti-technology and anti-state views.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Untraceable payment is a modern question; naturians reject state control but also modern technology, so no side follows.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; freedom from state control fits but the internet is technological.

person-over-state.rationale: Individualist anarchists reject treating persons as means for the community; the state is rejected entirely.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Zisly states naturians are all materialists.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is an industrial technology opposed to natural living.

dense-cities.rationale: Zisly urged a return to natural, open-air rural life, which clearly implies rejecting the claim, though the sources speak of natural living rather than comparing environmental impacts.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: They reject armies altogether so the statement's premise is not accepted.

language-defines-nation.rationale: National unification is not their aim.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy nationalism contrary to their outlook.

pollution-taxes.rationale: They oppose industrial pollution but also taxation by the state.

future-generations.rationale: Nature-centred critique of civilization supports preserving the Earth.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The naturian sources make no claims about distinct values of women.

arms-reduction.rationale: Opposes armed state power but wants abolition rather than reduction.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: They oppose legally established power and its monopolies.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Anarchist opposition to state war and military power implies refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Not stated for naturians; anarchist circles in Spain used syndicalist bargaining but naturians focused on lifestyle.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: State welfare and taxation they reject.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Legal rules by the state they reject.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: International economic rules are not addressed by the naturian sources.

smash-state-machine.rationale: They oppose all legally established power, which implies dismantling the state; some members were revolutionaries.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Naturians included both nomadic and sedentary, both communal and individual lifestyles, implying tolerance for varied arrangements.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Treating nature as a commodity contradicts their view that people should adapt to nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Materialists and anarchists reject the sacred nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans are a modern state-credit issue the sources never touch.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation within states is not discussed in the naturian sources.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Their appeal to natural law and a natural state implies a common nature; not redesigned by civilization.

public-service-media.rationale: State-funded media; they reject state institutions.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement; rejection is inferred from its anti-state and anti-industrial views.

workers-own-party.rationale: They oppose all politics, including parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not documented for naturians; anarchists oppose bodily coercion though they also reject legal power, so only inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance law is not discussed, and naturians reject legal property rules, so no documented stance exists.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A linguistic classification question with no connection to naturian writings.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Chiefs in lawmaking are a legal power.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Zisly's stress on natural life concerns freedom too; anarchists reject coercion for environment.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: State punishment itself is rejected by their anarchism, which clearly implies rejecting fixed sentences; not stated.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: A state-imposed requirement conflicts with their opposition to legal power, but the sources never mention immigration policy, so this is inferred.

voter-id.rationale: They reject elections and state identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: They reject religion and legal recognition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Naturist anarchists resisted church and state authority over the body, and no source shows them policing sex; inferred.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: The internet postdates the movement; rejection is inferred from its anti-state stance.

women-suffrage.rationale: They reject voting politics, though they would not deny women participation.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Zisly rejects religion, but no source links it to women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Naturian writings do not discuss racial categories.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; individual claims versus anarchist views of property are not settled.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Legal power at an international level.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Constitutional arrangements for Indigenous or national groups are not addressed by the naturian sources.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Defending a bureaucratic planned state is a Trotskyist-era question; rejection is inferred from the naturiens' hostility to the state and industrial planning.

national-church-status.rationale: They reject religion and state privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Decentralist sympathies but they reject territorial states; not addressed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Naturians rejected legally established power as coercive, but Zisly records revolutionaries among them, so an absolute ban on initiating force is not a documented naturian rule; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency as the heart of a return to natural life.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The sources do not address it; naturians rejected states and politics, so a vote on which state rules is outside their concern; inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Naturians rejected states and legal powers, so inherited borders would carry no weight; they did not campaign on borders; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Naturians rejected authorities and their restrictions, though they valued life close to nature; inferred from anarchism.

equal-conscription.rationale: Naturians rejected military power and the state, and Zisly's circle opposed militarism, so 'or neither' applies and men-only conscription is rejected.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Naturians loved nature and the land but rejected nations and states; whether a duty to guard ancestral land follows is inferred and unclear.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Naturians rejected all legal power and held to natural law; state killing without trial is inferred to be condemned.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment is not addressed by a current opposed to all states and politics; inferred as indifferent.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Naturians rejected states and nationalism, so a state supporting co-nationals abroad is inferred to be opposed.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Naturians called for free communities returning to nature and rejected property-based power; common claims on land and resources are inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: Individual freedom from all legal power and the right to live naked and self-sufficient imply authority over one's own body; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Naturians wanted limited needs and rejected state power, so lower consumption taxes are inferred to be welcome; taxes are not discussed.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Naturians rejected state programmes entirely and had no stated view on how to target them; inferred as indifferent.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Naturians rejected politics and all legally established power, including leaders, so rule by a leader is inferred to be opposed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Opposition to all legal power and to industrial civilization implies opposing state favours to industry; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Naturians rejected politics altogether and were materialists, so politics divided by religion is inferred to be opposed.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Naturians condemned machines and industrial progress, so combining advanced technology with tradition would not satisfy them.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anarchist naturists favoured free unions and rejected legal authority over relationships; inferred, as divorce is not discussed.

national-resource-control.rationale: Naturians rejected states and nations as owners; resources are inferred to belong to free communities, not national governments.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Naturians left property and distribution questions unaddressed; adherents' anarchism and simple living give no clear lean either way, so this is a split inference.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from their rejection of all legal power and politics: a state-imposed levy on finance would be an exercise of power they refused.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Race and advancement of disadvantaged groups do not appear in the sources, and nothing in their principles settles the question.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: They rejected every legally established power and accepted only the laws of nature, so human-made unjust law has no claim on conscience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Zisly and the naturians condemned machines and industrial progress as domineering, so maximising automation is the opposite of their aim.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: they opposed all concentrated power but wrote nothing on world order, so no side is clearly implied.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from their materialist, anti-capitalist anarchism that treats labour as the source of wealth; the sources do not discuss value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from anarchist rejection of states and nations; they did not discuss patriotism as such.

material-over-identity.rationale: The sources are silent on the left's priorities; naturians were concerned with natural life rather than left strategy.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: They refused all legal power and politics, so a party-led state of any kind, with or without markets, is incompatible with their anarchism.

missingStatements.text: People should live as simply and self-sufficiently as possible, keeping their needs limited.
missingStatements.rationale: Zisly promoted limited needs and self-sufficiency as the heart of a return to natural life.

missingStatements.text: Nudity in appropriate public settings is healthy and should be legally allowed.
missingStatements.rationale: Zisly defended nudism and naturist anarchists treated it as emancipatory, as Koch used it against authority.
missingStatements.declined: Too narrow: a single naturist practice that few other ideologies take a position on.

missingStatements.text: Machines and large-scale technology are inherently domineering over people.
missingStatements.rationale: Zisly saw machines as fundamentally domineering and opposed industrialization.

notes: Strands differed on diet (vegetarian and omnivore), settlement (nomadic and sedentary) and revolution, per Zisly. Spanish and Cuban anarchist naturism and German left naturism (Koch) are related but not the same current.
